text:
Right, lets give these two questions a shot. Firstly I'll add the caveat that I'm no expert and this is just what I believe is happening from what I've learned so far. To be honest, most things have started falling in to place in the last few weeks for me, I started looking at the questions as we already have all of the answers.

So first question ' Hi robbie, can you expain more with IF's chart about 'engulf, return to source of move'? and why price 'had hit its target'?'

In IF's chart I believe the first blue box is the FLAG, the red box isn't the FL of this FLAG, this is an important point to remember. A FL in the past held that flag up and the break of the FL in the past creates a new FL holding price down. Bearing this in mind, the last blue box is our new FL, holding price up.

So, we've left our FLAG with an engulf, before carrying on towards the FL below (we're in a FL PAZ so we want the other side) but before we can carry on we need to go back to the source of our engulf, the RBD that caused the drop. After returning to our source we then engulf the previous low, creating the FL/FTR.

Jumping ahead, we engulf the upper limit of the red box, our FL FTR. It's no surprise we've looking for the same simple thing, we've engulfed so price wants to go back to the source of the move, the decision.

Why had price hit it's target? When we engulfed the engulf of our red FL we created a new FL. The decision to engulf and create this new FL and enter the PAZ above was the source of the move and was where the orders were as strong upward movement from the source shows.

There were other things to indicate we were going to return to this point. Price move in to CP above and then broke the source(FL) of the move in to the CP making our blue FL the target.

Effex, did my answer to the other question answer your as well?

EDIT: I'm just going to add, I can tell I'm learning as there are a lot more confirmed trades on there than I have mentioned with great RR.

Hi all, I'm really starting to question the way flags are drawn now. It seems fine to determine one limit of the flag, for instance, if price is moving higher, breaks some SR supply and creatres an FTR/DBD we have one limit but what determines the next limit, is it the flag limit above? this doesn't work out, the only explanation can be that when prices returns to the FL/FTR which is created after breaking something significant, the previous high or low becomes the other flag boundary. It seems misleading saying that the flag limit above and below are the boundaries to the flag. the second limit can only be created after price has returned to the first limit? Does that make sense? So, this is why price returns to the base of a pole when the first limit of the flag is broken. I'll investigate more tomorrow.
